confidence_notes: I checked typical food and drink prices with web searches. Restaurant meals, coffee and beer come from third-party cost-of-living aggregators, some of which cite Numbeo. These include Pacific Prime in 2026, MyLifeElsewhere in 2026 and Traveltables in 2023. I could not reach Numbeo's own Tainan page, and the sources disagree: one listed an inexpensive meal at about USD 13 while the others put it at USD 3.50-5. I treated that higher figure as an outlier. Beer is set slightly above the aggregator range of USD 2.90-3.25 because sit-down restaurant servings in July 2026 tend to cost more. Cocktail and wine evidence was thin. Search found only individual bar listings: about 11 per cocktail with no currency shown, OpenTable bars tagged 'NT$999 and under', and minimum spends of NT$300-500. There was also a Taipei benchmark of about NT$400 per cocktail. The cocktail estimate of about NT$350-380 draws on those listings and its usual relationship to beer price. I found no per-glass wine price for Tainan, so the wine estimate of about NT$250-280 is based on its usual relationship to beer and cocktail prices, and it is the most uncertain drink anchor. I did not search for any accommodation prices. All four accommodation anchors are general-knowledge model estimates for Tainan in the July 2026 summer and school-holiday period, so they are less certain than the restaurant anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Tainan is a mid-sized city in southern Taiwan with a lot of domestic tourism. Its prices are generally a little below Taipei and close to Kaohsiung. I used Kaohsiung and a discounted Taipei as cross-checks, especially for drinks and accommodation.
